public_observable_parity.state_at_target_time: Solution y(t) evaluated via integrate(tout) must match pinned native within specified rtol and atol (max rel err < 1e-4 for stiff problems, < 1e-6 for analytic)
public_observable_parity.one_step_advancement: step(tout) must advance by one internal BDF step and return the new internal time tn, advancing monotonically towards tout
public_observable_parity.derivative_evaluation: derivative(tout, n) must match numerical derivatives and native CVodeGetDky to within BDF interpolation error
public_observable_parity.forward_sensitivity: sensitivity(k, p) must match analytic derivatives and native CVodeGetSens for parameterized ODEs
public_observable_parity.limits_and_configuration: Tolerances, max_step, min_step, max_steps, and max_err_test_fails must be strictly enforced with source-equivalent error exceptions
public_observable_parity.reinitialization: Calling reinitialize(t0, func) must clear history so subsequent solves are completely uncontaminated by prior runs

numerical_behavior.stiff_stability: Must integrate stiff problems (Robertson kinetics, stiff exponential decay lambda=1e6) stably without unphysical oscillations
numerical_behavior.tolerance_response: Tightening rtol from 1e-4 down to 1e-10 must show expected error reduction
numerical_behavior.bdf_orders: Must support and exercise variable BDF orders 1 through 5
numerical_behavior.long_horizon: Must integrate over long time horizons (> 1000 time units) without artificial limit failures when configured with reasonable max_steps

internal_solver_behavior.step_sequences: Because Python BDF and native SUNDIALS use adaptive step heuristics, internal step sizes and orders need not be bit-for-bit identical, provided trajectories and public observables match the contract
